title.value: You Only Live Once: Single-Life Reinforcement Learning
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper which is the concept of Single-Life Reinforcement Learning (SLRL), a new reinforcement learning setting.
title.quote: Title of the paper: You Only Live Once: Single-Life Reinforcement Learning

extractions.description: This paper introduces and formalizes a new problem setting called Single-Life Reinforcement Learning (SLRL), where an agent must successfully complete a task within a single trial by leveraging prior experience and adapting to novel situations autonomously. The paper proposes a distribution matching strategy, Q-weighted adversarial learning (Q WALE), to improve the agent's performance in SLRL compared to traditional reinforcement learning methods. The authors provide experimental results showing the effectiveness of Q WALE in various single-life continuous control problems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses the application of Single-Life Reinforcement Learning in contexts like disaster relief, the central focus is on the development and testing of reinforcement learning algorithms rather than sustainability or ecological aspects. The example of a disaster relief robot is mentioned to illustrate the SLRL concept, not to directly address sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Reinforcement learning algorithms are typically designed to learn a performant policy that can repeatedly and autonomously complete a task, usually starting from scratch. However, in many real-world situations, the goal might not be to learn a policy that can do the task repeatedly, but simply to perform a new task successfully once in a single trial.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on a new reinforcement learning algorithm and does not directly tackle themes related to ecological or climate-related sustainable development. Although it uses disaster relief as a scenario, this serves more as an illustration rather than a central theme related to sustainability.
primary_category.quote: The vast range of situations that could be encountered at test time cannot be anticipated in advance during training, and therefore agents that can adapt at test time will be better equipped to cope with new situations.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not address secondary Climate or Ecologically-Related Sustainable Development themes as its main focus is on reinforcement learning algorithm development.
secondary_categories.quote: We propose an algorithm, Q-weighted adversarial learning (Q WALE), which employs a distribution matching strategy that leverages the agent’s prior experience as guidance in novel situations.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific ecological or climate-related sub-category is directly applicable to this paper. The focus is on machine learning and reinforcement learning challenges rather than environmental or sustainable development concerns.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our contributions are as follows. We formalize the SLRL problem setting, which provides a natural setting in which to study autonomous adaptation to novel situations in reinforcement learning.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper is not focused on specific sub-categories related to ecological or climate concerns. It primarily deals with reinforcement learning methodology.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We propose a new approach, Q-weighted adversarial learning (Q WALE), which is less sensitive to the quality of prior data available and provides the agent with a shaped reward towards completing the desired task a single time.

applications.justification: This application is mentioned as an example of where Single-Life Reinforcement Learning could be useful, illustrating a real-world scenario where the algorithm could be tested and used.
applications.quote: For example, imagine a disaster relief robot tasked with retrieving an item from a fallen building, where it cannot get direct supervision from humans.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is fundamentally about advancements in reinforcement learning algorithms, which fits better under the category of Machine Learning & AI Research rather than any specific sustainability category.
new_primary_category.quote: Our experiments on several single-life continuous control problems indicate that methods based on our distribution matching formulation are 20-60% more successful because they can more quickly recover from novel states.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The core contribution of the paper is the development and testing of a new reinforcement learning framework and algorithm, which fits under this specific sub-category in AI research.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Motivated by this observation, we propose an algorithm, Q-weighted adversarial learning (Q WALE), which employs a distribution matching strategy that leverages the agent’s prior experience as guidance in novel situations.
